前提・単位・境界 周期y方向のky=4に制限した2D場、c=1。板[4,5]のε∞=1.5、Δε=0.75、ω0=9、γ=0.5、σ=0.04。外側は真空、PEC端は[-24,36]、T=60です。 編集上の補足 任意の横方向分布ではなく単一kyの実空間制限です。1つの受動Lorentz極と有限帯域・有限窓のみ。Gaussian尾は厳密には非零で、窓診断と参照誤差を別記します。 全周波数で厳密にcap反射が未到達という証明ではありません。 周期y方向の1周期を表示しています。波形を見やすくするため、x軸とy軸の表示縮尺は異なります。 採用した計算法 単一ky Yee空間演算と局所の陰的中点Lorentz ADE。p偏光の両電場に分極を結合し、同格子の真空波束で入射・伝播位相を除きます。直接Ohmic・物質減衰仕事と修正エネルギーを別々に集計します。 Registry and counting notes These additional validation supplements are managed separately from the common 22-example registry. Receipts cover independent ZIP extraction, tests and every fixed input within each group. Changes of settings, methods or step sizes do not add independent physical problems. Results and verificationMethods, equations, figures and references Assumptions, units and boundaries Use a two-dimensional field restricted to periodic transverse wave number ky = 4 and c = 1. The slab [4, 5] has epsilon_inf = 1.5, delta_epsilon = 0.75, omega_0 = 9, gamma = 0.5 and sigma = 0.04. Outer vacuum ends at PEC caps [-24, 36]; T = 60. Editorial clarification This is a genuine single-ky restriction rather than arbitrary transverse data. It covers one passive Lorentz pole and a fixed finite band/window. Gaussian tails are nonzero; window diagnostics and reference errors are reported separately. No strict all-frequency no-return proof is claimed. One transverse y period is shown. The displayed x and y scales differ to make the fields visible. Adopted numerical method Use the single-ky Yee spatial operator and local implicit-midpoint Lorentz ADE. Couple both p-polarized electric components to polarization, and remove incident propagation with a matched vacuum pulse on the same grid. Accumulate direct Ohmic and material-damping work separately from modified energy. ε∞∂tE=∇×H−σE−J,∂tP=Jε∞​∂t​E=∇×H−σE−J,∂t​P=J ∂tJ=fE−ω02P−γJ,f=Δεω02∂t​J=fE−ω02​P−γJ,f=Δεω02​ ε(ω)=ε∞+fω02−ω2−iγω+iσωε(ω)=ε∞​+ω02​−ω2−iγωf​+ωiσ​ References and measured quantities Measure omega = 5.1/6/6.9 from 12 actual material/vacuum evolutions across three resolutions and both polarizations. Check an independent finite-window vacuum geometric sum, complex Fresnel coefficients, direct volume dissipation, all-step PEC budgets and final monitor tails.
